title: Dominant pullbacks, refinements and finite covers in the alteration topology
statement:
Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a prime $\ell$. In $\operatorname{alt}/S$ with the topology of $\ell'$-alterations, finite covering families can be composed and a family refining a covering by coverings is covering. Every covering sieve contains a finite covering family. Fibre products in this category are obtained by taking the reduced union of the components of the usual fibre product which dominate components of the base. Pullback in this sense preserves covering families. The same base-change operation along a dominant finite-type map of integral Noetherian schemes preserves alteration covering families on the integral target, using components dominating the new base. A proper surjective generically finite morphism of integral Noetherian schemes of generic degree prime to $\ell$ is a singleton covering, as is a proper birational morphism. Finite affine open covers are covering. On reduced schemes the finite family of their reduced irreducible components is covering. An object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ is reduced and finite type over $S$, with all generic points mapping to generic points and inducing finite residue-field extensions.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-irreducible-components].
